title: Dynamic curve · Construction of simple curves
slide_intent: Teach designers to place an arc according to the space the mark needs. Moving the center changes where the field opens and therefore where the eye can find the identifier.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can preserve the circular source of the curve across formats while reserving a wider area on the right for its standard mark.
demonstration: Two upright rectangles share an off-center axis. Cyan arcs, dotted radii and an X-to-2X width division show their circular construction. Smaller diagrams extend the construction to a square detail and a horizontal format.
practical_value: Locate the circle axis one part into a three-part width in the illustrated construction. Check the protected field at the right before placing the standard mark.

content_islands.name: Heading and rationale
content_islands.spec: Set the red device name above the gray construction title. Place the short explanation beside the diagrams at left.

content_islands.name: Upright construction
content_islands.spec: Stack two vertical frames around a shared center point. Extend the top and bottom arcs outside the frames, shade the isolated fields and mark the off-center axis with X and 2X below.

content_islands.name: Circle and format comparison
content_islands.spec: At right, pair a small complete circle around a frame with a wide rectangular frame below. Use cyan callouts to explain the source geometry and its use on different formats.
